citations.field: PDF p. 613, printed p. 600; headword 旳(的), plus continuation on PDF p. 614, printed p. 601
citations.text: I inspected both supplied scans. The headword is 旳(的), with readings dī and dí; its entry continues on the next page. The text classifies it as a phonosemantic graph and quotes Shuowen: “的，明也。从日，勺声.” It reports the “的然” example from Liji Zhongyong, interprets 的颡 as a horse with a white forehead, and says 的 is used for white while 卢 denotes black in 的卢. It sends other senses to separate 的 entries. These are the book author’s claims, not independent confirmation of the proposed semantic history.
citations.title: 說文解字「旳」 — Shuowen.org; compare its transcription with 字源

citations.field: PDF p. 613, printed p. 600; headword 旳(的), pronunciation lines, and PDF p. 614 / printed p. 601 continuation; inspected supplied scan pixels
citations.text: The p. 613 headword is 旳(的), with dī and dí pronunciation lines, followed by specimens labeled Shuowen small seal and Han 的 clerical forms. On p. 614 the continuation quotes Shuowen’s “的，明也。从日，勺声” and separately explains 旳顙 as a white-foreheaded horse, reporting that the graph is also written with an unidentified printed character and discussing 的卢. These are the book author’s claims; they do not establish the graphic transition’s date or mechanism. I directly inspected both supplied page images. The printed page numbers 600 and 601 are visible.
citations.title: 《字源》, ed. Li Xueqin, 2012, PDF pp. 613–614 / printed pp. 600–601; compare 說文解字「旳」

citations.field: PDF p. 613, printed p. 600; headword and pronunciation lines; directly inspected attached scan pixels
citations.text: The headword is 旳(的). Its two pronunciation lines are dī and dí, and each prints 端组、药部; 端组、锡韵、都历切. The scan also labels specimens as Shuowen small seal and Han clerical forms. These observations report this edition’s print, not the general current reading of 旳 or an ancient reconstruction.
